note: THE PROOF-OF-PROGRESS LEDGER for the BN4 legs -- the speedrun route's
FIRST three completions (bn4.1, bn4.2, bn4.3), of which only leg-bn4.1 has
ever been measured.
FIRST MEASUREMENT (2026-08-29). Before this file, `leg-bn4.1` had never run
past ten virtual minutes: every run in runs/ was a smoke with lastT between
45s and 600s, there was no `bench:sim:leg-bn4.1` script and no BN4 lane. The
route's own first leg was its least-covered one. These numbers are the first
evidence it has.
WHAT THIS LEG IS. A genuinely fresh BN4: 8 GB home, $1,000, no Source-Files.
Singularity is node-native, which is why the route starts here and why
nothing is injected. BN4 is also the hardest possible opening --
WorldDaemonDifficulty 3 puts the daemon at hacking 9000 (three times BN1)
while ScriptHackMoney 0.2 x ServerMaxMoney 0.1125 leaves hacking earning
~2% of BN1, HackExpGain is 0.4, and hacknet/crime/company money are 0.05 /
0.2 / 0.1. Stocks and coding contracts are the only unnerfed money channels.
NO LIKE-FOR-LIKE TARGET EXISTS. The historical 17d run
(spec/strategy/speedrun-benchmark.md) did 4.1 in 14h15m, but it entered BN4
holding SF1.1 earned in a 21-minute manual BN1. This leg enters with
nothing, so 14h15m is a reference point, not a target to miss.
Each entry is the BEST result we have actually observed on that profile, not
a target and not a guess. Some of these numbers are FAILURES; they are here
because a failure you have measured is the starting point of the next
improvement.
RULES.
1. Only ever move a number in the improving direction, and only from a run
you actually observed. Never relax one to make a red run green.
2. `timeToGoalHours` and `firstInstallHours` improve DOWNWARD.
`augmentationsAt`, `installs` and `reached` improve UPWARD.
3. `provenance` pins the simulator semantics these numbers were measured
under. Bumping SIMULATOR_MODEL_VERSION or the vendored commit changes
what the simulator DOES, so old numbers stop being comparable.
HOW TO RE-MEASURE. Cheaper than BN1 -- a money-starved node runs fewer
scripts, so 24 virtual hours costs ~11 wall minutes rather than hours:
bun run long bn4                             # the validity smoke, 15 vmin
bun run bench:sim:leg-bn4.1                  # the benchmark, seeds 1-3
bun run sim -- --profile leg-bn4.1 --seed 3 --horizon 72h --compact --perf

leg-bn4.1.note: NOT REACHED on any seed in 24h. These are the FIRST numbers taken from a controller that runs the whole horizon: every earlier measurement of this leg was truncated by the ns-proxy deadlock at 21-24h (see openDefects). Seed 3 is the deep one -- 6 installs, 31 augs, hacking 681, $55.9b, 45.81h of route ETA remaining at the horizon. 2026-08-29 (model 11, diagnosis): the 21-24h stop is a controller deadlock, not a strategy outcome. The ns-proxy resident needs a 162.1 GB placement (a 160 GB declared union of batched calls) that no host can hold, and #respawn retries it forever while the controller awaits it. Every telemetry topic goes silent 2.1h before the horizon while the engine completes all 432,000 cycles.

First install 1.067h (s3), second 4.790h (s1). Zero resident warnings.
leg-bn4.1.measuredUnder: --perf, post-deadlock-fix. Telemetry-on reproduces --perf exactly since the seeded-stream fix, so the mode no longer changes the result.

openDefects.what: `--perf` (telemetry off) and the ordinary telemetry build played measurably different games from the same seed, which AGENTS.md forbids: 'A --perf build must be behaviourally identical to a telemetry build -- only quieter.' On leg-bn4.1 seed 3 at a 30h horizon, --perf reached 6 installs / 35 augs / hacking 867 / 16.12h route ETA while telemetry on reached 2 installs / 24 augs / hacking 379 / 151.18h.
openDefects.cause: `initTelemetry` built its run id from `Math.random()` (game/lib/telemetry.ts). The simulator replaces `Math.random` with the run's SEEDED stream (sim/realm/timers.ts:168), so that single draw shifted every later random number in the process. Each mode stayed internally deterministic, which is why the divergence read as a strategy result rather than as a seed shift.
openDefects.fix: The run id is now derived from `shortIdentity(identity.install.id)` -- state the run already holds, no RNG, still unique. Verified: telemetry-on and --perf now agree EXACTLY at a 30h horizon, prestiges [1.067, 5.036, 8.742, 11.561, 19.706, 21.363] and identical installs/augs/hacking/trades/route ETA. Pinned by tests/telemetry-client.test.ts, which asserts initTelemetry takes ZERO draws and fails on the old line.
openDefects.impactOnRecordedEvidence: NONE, and this is the important correction. The unshifted stream is the --perf one, and every route-leg baseline in this repo was recorded under --perf, so no recorded number moves. The bug was also inert in the real game, where `Math.random` is not seeded. What it broke was comparability: any simulator run taken with telemetry on -- a UI-attached run, a dashboard session -- was not comparable to the --perf benchmarks it would be read against.

openDefects.what: DIAGNOSED. leg-bn4.1 does not stall on strategy -- the CONTROLLER LOOP STOPS. At t~21.9h the ns-proxy resident `nsp` needs a 162.1 GB placement that no host in the fleet can hold, and `NsProxy.#respawn` (game/lib/ns-proxy.ts:528-605) retries it in an unbounded `for(;;)` loop. The controller awaits that call, so it never completes another pass: every telemetry topic goes silent at 21.89-21.97h with hours of horizon left, no installs happen, no augmentations are bought, and the published route ETA freezes at its last value. The run stays `valid` with no crashes and no unmodeled calls, because nothing actually fails -- it waits forever.
evidence: The run prints it: sim.result `output` carries `WARNING: ns resident nsp cannot be PLACED at all (needs 162.1GB) -- retrying; no host in the fleet has that much free.` and the same at 82.1 GB earlier.
Every topic stops publishing at once, 2.1 hours before the horizon: progression 21.97h, arbitration 21.97h, factions 21.95h, career 21.91h, player 21.89h, endgame.route 21.70h, against a 24h horizon.

The engine is fine -- engineCycles=432000 is exactly 24h of 200ms cycles. Already-dispatched work continues without the controller: charisma 575 -> 711 and money $54.3b -> $56.6b after it goes silent, while hacking (+12), installs, augmentations and stock trades are frozen.

Reproduced by a probe matching the CLI exactly (label, profile, experiment, goFidelity, allowBitNodeCompletion): prestiges [1.067, 5.036, 8.742, 11.561, 19.706, 21.363], identical to bench:sim:leg-bn4.1.
openDefects.suspect: Not yet isolated, and note it must be re-established under whichever mode survives openDefects/perf-build-plays-a-different-game: the freeze above is a property of the --perf trajectory. A filtered telemetry-on probe of the same leg did NOT reproduce it -- there faction reputation accrues steadily (The Black Hand 3,188 -> 162,927 rep over 19.2h-24.25h) toward a 7-augmentation package -- but that probe is a different trajectory for the same reason.
openDefects.nextStep: Two candidate fixes, and the choice is a design decision in a load-bearing subsystem rather than a bolt-on. (1) Chunk the declared union: unlike a single indivisible call, a 160 GB union of many calls can be split into placeable batches, which is the direct fix. (2) Bound the retry: `#respawn` should not spin forever on a requirement no host can ever satisfy -- it should surface a blocker the way factions does for the 80 GB SingularityFn3 wall (shared/strategy/factions/decide.ts:379), so the run fails loudly instead of going quiet. Doing (2) alone would turn a silent stall into a diagnosable one without unblocking the leg.
openDefects.cause: TWO defects in `game/lib/ns-proxy.ts`, compounding. (1) `#guaranteeFit` capped what it ASKED for at MAX_ASK_GB (64) while demanding the uncapped priced sum, so the arena reserved 65.6 GB for a respawn that would accept nothing under 162.1 GB -- ask and demand could never meet. (2) `priceCall` returned the 80 GB `UNKNOWN_CALL_GB` fallback whenever `getFunctionRamCost` threw, which includes the transient case where `nsMain()` is momentarily unpublished (it is, across a prestige -- the first 162.1 GB demand lands in the same instant as the third install). The union sums that guess once PER member, so the two-path dnet `guaranteeFit` demanded 2 x 80 = 160 GB for calls that really cost 0.05 and 1.3 GB.
openDefects.whyItIsADeadlock: The controller needs the placement to act; the placement needs free fleet RAM; freeing it means buying a bigger server, which is `hacking:infrastructure:ram` wanting $3.16t and DENIED (`reason: outbid`, `available: 0`) while stock holds the bankroll as working capital; and issuing that purchase requires the controller, which is blocked. Nothing in the loop can break the cycle, which is why it survives to a 120h horizon.
openDefects.fix: `priceOf` now reports whether the runtime actually gave a price, so a GUESS can inform the ask but never becomes an unsatisfiable floor; a partly-guessed union is held to what a resident can be granted, while a fully-priced one keeps its floor however large, because those calls genuinely cannot run in less. `#guaranteeFit` now raises the ask to cover its own floor. And `#respawn` gained the failure exit it never had: a minute of unbroken refusal is declared impossible and throws, emitting `proxy.impossible`, so a demand the fleet cannot meet becomes a fault a feature can report instead of a silent halt that takes the whole controller with it. Pinned by tests/ns-proxy.test.ts and tests/ram-budget.test.ts.
openDefects.result: leg-bn4.1 seed 3 at a 30h horizon: prestiges [1.067, 5.036, 8.742, 11.561, 17.99, 23.087, 25.603, 26.239] against [1.067, 5.036, 8.742, 11.561, 19.706, 21.363] before -- three installs past the old freeze point, 8 installs against 6, hacking 947 against 867, 1,183 stock trades against 632, $2.6t cash against $75b, and ZERO resident placement warnings where there were 12,908 undersized refusals.

openDefects.what: The `daedalus reputation` route leg is `measured: false` on every seed at the horizon, at 4.2h/26.5h/42.7h, and is the largest remaining term on seeds 1 and 2. bn1.json names the same wall for BN1: 'the Daedalus favor-unlock reputation leg at a measured-but-starved work rate (factions loses the slot)'. It is therefore not a BN4 problem, but BN4 is where it decides the leg.
openDefects.evidence: strategy.routeParts in all three seeds' sim.result
openDefects.nextStep: Attack it as a factions/arbiter question, not a BN4 one; a fix moves both legs.

openDefects.what: Enabling dnet on BN4's surface exposed a high-volume dispatch refusal: 9,693 refusal incidents on seed 1 alone, 64,283 across seeds 2-3, spanning 1,904 distinct darknet hosts. The wanted RAM is often BELOW the reported room (e.g. `phish x3 wanted 11.10GB, room 11.85GB`), yet `exec` returns 0. game/dnet/controller.ts already logs once per incident and treats `exec` returning 0 as ambiguous between a missing script, a host that cannot fit, and a refused darknet check -- so this may be the session check rather than RAM. It did not invalidate any run.
openDefects.evidence: the `[dnet] launch refused` lines in the seeds 1-3 bench logs
openDefects.nextStep: Decide whether the refusals cost throughput or are ordinary darknet-host churn (hosts mutate, so new hostnames are expected). If they are real, `durableRoomGb` and the engine disagree about what fits.

openDefects.status: OPEN, found while re-measuring after the deadlock fix
openDefects.what: A 24h leg-bn4.1 seed crashed Bun outright -- `panic(main thread): Segmentation fault`, RSS 58.69 GB, peak 0.07 TB, after 1,553s. Seeds 1 and 3 of the same batch completed valid; seed 2 died. An earlier dnet-off control run died the same way (exit 133). REPRODUCED: a second 30h seed-3 run reached 59.87 GB RSS on the same trajectory and was killed before it could segfault. It is not caused by the ns-proxy fix -- it reproduces on the reviewed code and on the code before it -- but it now BLOCKS verification, because a full-horizon leg run is the only way to check the leg end to end and it does not reliably survive one.
openDefects.whyItSurfacedNow: Probably not new. Before the ns-proxy fix these runs wedged at ~21h and coasted doing almost nothing, so they never reached the memory the working controller needs. A run that actually keeps deciding for 24 virtual hours is a much heavier run.
openDefects.nextStep: Profile a long run's heap (`bun run sim:profile --cpu-prof` has a sampler; the equivalent for allocation is what is needed). spec/simulator.md already records that run cost grows with run length (-77% throughput decay across a 24h run) and calls it the simulator's historically worst class of bug; this looks like the same lead reaching its conclusion. Until it is fixed a 3-seed 24h batch is not reliably completable on this machine.
